question.problem:
The parabola $y=-{x}^{2}+3x+15$ and the line $y=4x-5$ intersect at the points $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2}),$ where ${x}_{1}<{x}_{2}.$ Find the values of ${x}_{1}$ and  ${x}_{2}.$

${x}_{1}=$
{{field-1}}$,\,{x}_{2}=$
{{field-2}}
question.worked_solution:
We need to solve the following system consisting of the equations of the curves:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}y=-{x}^{2}+3x+15 \\ y=4x-5\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the equations equal to one another and solving, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+3x+15 & =4x-5 \\ -{x}^{2}-x+20 & =0 \\ -({x}^{2}+x-20) & =0 \\ -(x+5)(x-4) & =0 \\ x & =-5,4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the $x$-coordinates of the intersection points are ${x}_{1}=-5$ and ${x}_{2}=4.$
